summation.displayName: In response to mechanical loading, the integrin alphaVbeta3 ...
summation.text:
In response to mechanical loading, the integrin alphaVbeta3 (ITGAV:ITGB3) complex located in the dendritic plasma membrane of osteocytes positively regulates activation (phosphorylation) of AKT1 via phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) and, presumably, its product phosphatidylinositol-3,4,5-trisphosphate (PIP3) (inferred from mouse homologs).
Integrin alphaVbeta3 binds osteopontin of the extracellular matrix (inferred from chicken homologs in Ross et al. 1993) in a punctate pattern along the osteocyte dendrite (inferred from mouse cells in McNamara et al. 2009). Electrical signaling is only observed at these punctate sites of attachment (inferred from mouse MLO-Y4 osteocyte-like cells in Wu et al. 2011) therefore connections between integrins and the extracellular matrix appear to be required for integrin signaling.
AKT1 is phosphorylated on both tyrosine-308 and serine-473 (inferred from mouse homologs). Osteocytes predominantly contain AKT1 and very little AKT2 or AKT3 (inferred from mice in Batra et al. 2014, reviewed in Mao et al. 2023).
